Description: Late at night, Tony Dauer knocks on Annie Beaumont’s Attic door, shows her the pocket watch he stole, and tries to hide it to avoid implicating his mother. Annie immediately turns on him, demands the watch, and threatens to tell on him. Their relationship collapses quickly, and Tony leaves in anger.
Location: Attic（Attic）
Key Information:
  - Tony Dauer knocks on the Attic door again and demands Annie open it; Annie initially refuses strongly to let him in.
  - Tony says “I’ve got something you’ll find very interesting,” prompting Annie to open the door; the two then confront each other in the Attic.
  - Annie immediately judges the item Tony brought (the pocket watch) is valuable and presses him for where it came from.
  - Tony admits he stole the pocket watch and explains it is related to the “stranger” who appeared in the villa.
  - Tony says the stranger is looking for someone named “Rupert Galley,” but no one in the Living room knows who that is.
  - Annie adds: after Tony left, Oswald came to the Attic and she referred to him as “that old man.”
  - Oswald has a funny little mustache.
  - Tony says he once saw the name “Rupert Galley” written on a small box in his mother’s room, and that his mother showed it to him once before he came upstairs.
  - Tony believes the stranger may be looking for the pocket watch, so he plans to hide it to avoid implicating his mother, and intentionally does not tell her.
  - Annie demands Tony hand over the pocket watch, claiming she will return it to Tony’s mother.
  - Tony refuses, and Annie switches to threatening: “I’ll tell your mom you stole it.”
  - Annie bluntly says she really needs the pocket watch, stressing they aren’t truly acquaintances and their opposing positions are now clear.
  - Tony angrily says he trusted Annie wrongly, warns her not to rat him out, and leaves.
  - Tony slams the door as he leaves; Annie calls after him but fails to stop him.
Characters:
  [Annie Beaumont（Annie Beaumont）] Person No. 2, inside the Attic room at night.
    · Initially refuses to let Tony into the Attic, but opens after he shows “something interesting.”
    · Quickly assesses the pocket watch’s value and questions its origin.
    · Demands Tony hand over the watch, claiming she will return it to his mother.
    · Threatens to tell his mother after he refuses, clearly stating she really needs the watch.
    · Tries to stop Tony from leaving after the argument escalates but fails.
  [Tony Dauer（Tony Dauer）] Person No. 4, Helen Dauer’s son, who comes to Annie carrying the pocket watch.
    · Knocks late at night, enters the Attic, and shows Annie the pocket watch.
    · Admits he stole it and says it was to avoid implicating his mother.
    · Mentions a stranger looking for “Rupert Galley” and believes the stranger may be after the watch.
    · Says he saw “Rupert Galley” written on a small box in his mother’s room and that she showed it to him once.
    · Refuses to hand over the watch and, after being threatened, leaves angrily, warning Annie not to tell.
